record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Let G be a right-orderable group and N be a nilpotent subgroup of G. Let P be a positive cone for some right order on G. Let N # be a minimal divisible completion of N and P # be the positive cone of a right order on N # which is an extension of the right order of N with positive cone P ∩ N. Let g ∈ N # and ≤g denote the right order on N induced by the right order of N # with positive cone (P # )g . Is ≤g extendable to a right order on G?

evidence.quote: 2.30∗ . (V. V. Bludov) Let G be a right-orderable group and N be a nilpotent subgroup of G. Let P be a positive cone for some right order on G. Let N # be a minimal divisible completion of N and P # be the positive cone of a right order on N # which is an extension of the right order of N with positive cone P ∩ N. artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called right-orderable if there exists a total order $\leq$ on $G$ that is invariant under right multiplication, i.e. $a \leq b$ implies $ac \leq bc$ for all $a,b,c \in G$. Equivalently, $G$ admits a positive cone, that is, a subset $P \subseteq G$ with $P \cdot P \subseteq P$, $P \cap P^{-1} = \emptyset$, and $P \cup P^{-1} = G \setminus \{e\}$; the associated right order is defined by $a < b \iff ba^{-1} \in P$. For $g \in G$, the conjugate cone $P^g := g^{-1} P g$ is again a positive cone of a right order on $G$.

A nilpotent group $N$ admits a minimal divisible completion $N^{\#}$: a divisible nilpotent group containing $N$ such that every element of $N^{\#}$ has some positive power lying in $N$, and which is minimal with this property.

Suppose $G$ is a right-orderable group with positive cone $P$ defining a right order on $G$, and let $N$ be a nilpotent subgroup of $G$. The intersection $P \cap N$ is the positive cone of the induced right order on $N$. Let $P^{\#}$ be a positive cone of a right order on the minimal divisible completion $N^{\#}$ of $N$ that extends this induced order, i.e.\ $P^{\#} \cap N = P \cap N$.

For an element $g \in N^{\#}$, consider the conjugate cone $(P^{\#})^g \subseteq N^{\#}$, and let $\leq_g$ denote the right order induced on $N$ by intersecting $(P^{\#})^g$ with $N$, i.e.\ the right order on $N$ with positive cone $(P^{\#})^g \cap N$.

Question: Must the right order $\leq_g$ on $N$ always extend to a right order on the whole group $G$?
